tools.name: list_playbooks
tools.description: List playbooks owned by or shared with the authenticated user, including access role and content counts.

tools.name: create_playbook
tools.description: Create a new playbook. A playbook is a container for personas (AI personalities), skills (capabilities), and memory (persistent storage).

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: Get a playbook with its singleton persona, skills, connected MCP servers, and memory.

tools.name: delete_playbook
tools.description: Delete a playbook and all its contents (personas, skills, memory, API keys). This action cannot be undone!

tools.name: create_persona
tools.description: Set the singleton persona (AI identity and system prompt) for a playbook. Backward-compatible alias for updating persona fields.

tools.name: update_persona
tools.description: Update a persona's name, system prompt, or metadata.

tools.name: delete_persona
tools.description: Reset the singleton persona to the default assistant. The playbook always retains one logical persona.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List all skills (capabilities/rules) in this playbook Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific skill Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: read_memory
tools.description: Read a specific memory entry by key. Automatically increments access count. Memory supports 3 tiers: 'working' (active scratch pad), 'contextual' (recent context), 'longterm' (archived). Use 'hierarchical' memory_type for complex task graphs with parallel threads. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: search_memory
tools.description: Search memories by text, tags, tier, or type. Returns summaries for large memories. Use tags for categorical search; use tier to focus on active vs archived data; use memory_type to find task graphs. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: write_memory
tools.description: Write a memory entry. Use tier='working' for active tasks, 'contextual' for background context, 'longterm' for completed work. Set memory_type='hierarchical' and parent_key to build task graphs. Use status to track task progress in parallel workflows. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: delete_memory
tools.description: Delete a memory entry (requires API key) Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: consolidate_memories
tools.description: Consolidate multiple related memories into a parent memory with summary. Reduces context size while preserving detail access via children. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: promote_memory
tools.description: Promote a memory to a higher tier or boost its priority for active use. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: get_memory_context
tools.description: Get a context-optimized view of memories. Returns full working memory, summaries for contextual, and keys only for longterm. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: archive_memories
tools.description: Archive memories from working/contextual to longterm tier. Useful for cleaning up after completing tasks. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: get_memory_tree
tools.description: Get hierarchical tree view of memories showing parent-child relationships. Use this to visualize task graphs and track parallel operations. Includes status for each node. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: create_task_graph
tools.description: Create a hierarchical task plan in one call. Creates a parent 'plan' memory with children for each subtask. Use this for complex multi-threaded work that agent swarms can coordinate on. Each subtask gets its own memory node with status tracking. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: update_task_status
tools.description: Update the status of a task node in a hierarchical plan. When all children of a parent are 'completed', the parent is auto-updated. Returns the current subtree state. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: list_canvas
tools.description: List canvas documents in a workflow run. Canvas documents are collaborative markdown files that multiple agents can edit in parallel. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: read_canvas
tools.description: Read a canvas document. Returns full content, sections structure, and metadata. Optionally read a specific section by ID. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: write_canvas
tools.description: Create or fully replace a canvas document. Markdown headings are auto-parsed into sections for parallel editing. Use patch_canvas_section for partial updates. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: patch_canvas_section
tools.description: Edit a specific section of a canvas document. Parallel-safe: only updates the targeted section. Lock the section first for safety in multi-agent scenarios. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: get_canvas_toc
tools.description: Get the table of contents for a canvas document. Returns section IDs, headings, and levels for navigation and patch_canvas_section. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: lock_canvas_section
tools.description: Lock a section for exclusive editing. Prevents other agents from modifying it. Remember to unlock when done. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: unlock_canvas_section
tools.description: Unlock a previously locked section so other agents can edit it. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: create_skill
tools.description: Create a new skill for this playbook. Use this to expand capabilities. Requires full or skills:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: update_skill
tools.description: Update an existing skill in this playbook. Requires full or skills:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: delete_skill
tools.description: Delete a skill from this playbook. Requires full or skills:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: list_skill_versions
tools.description: List historical versions of a skill for auditing or rollback. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: rollback_skill
tools.description: Rollback a skill to a previous version. Requires full or skills:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: update_playbook
tools.description: Update the persona/system prompt or the project instructions of this playbook. Handle with extreme care! Requires full or playbooks:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: list_mcp_servers
tools.description: List the MCP and OpenAPI servers connected to this playbook, including transport metadata and discovered capability counts. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: call_connected_tool
tools.description: Call a tool on one of this playbook's connected MCP servers. This stable wrapper lets the user control plane apply newly created playbooks without dynamically changing its own tool list. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: create_mcp_server
tools.description: Connect an MCP or OpenAPI server to this playbook. Requires playbooks:write or full permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: update_mcp_server
tools.description: Update a connected MCP or OpenAPI server. Requires playbooks:write or full permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: delete_mcp_server
tools.description: Disconnect an MCP or OpenAPI server from this playbook. Requires playbooks:write or full permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List workflow runs for this playbook. Runs isolate canvas artifacts and execution context. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: create_run
tools.description: Create a workflow run so this playbook can be applied immediately with isolated context and canvas artifacts. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: update_run
tools.description: Update a workflow run's name, status, or context. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: delete_run
tools.description: Delete a workflow run and its isolated canvas artifacts. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: list_secrets
tools.description: List all secret names and metadata in this playbook. Does NOT return values — secret values are never exposed to agents. Requires secrets:read permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: use_secret
tools.description: Make an HTTP request with a secret injected as a header. The secret value is NEVER returned to the agent — it is decrypted and used server-side only. Use this to authenticate API calls without exposing credentials. Example: use_secret({secret_name: 'OPENAI_API_KEY', url: 'https://api.openai.com/v1/m

tools.name: store_secret
tools.description: Store a new encrypted secret. The value is encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a per-user derived key and never stored or returned in plaintext. Requires secrets:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: rotate_secret
tools.description: Rotate (update) an existing secret with a new value. The old value is permanently replaced and cannot be recovered. Requires secrets:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

tools.name: delete_secret
tools.description: Permanently delete a secret. Cannot be undone. Requires secrets:write permission. Target a playbook with playbook_id.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "manage" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_memory, use_secret · Private data: delete_playbook, delete_memory, list_canvas, read_canvas, write_canvas, patch_canvas_section, get_canvas_toc, list_secrets, use_secret, store_secret, rotate_secret, delete_secret · Public sink: use_secret · Destructive: delete_playbook, delete_persona, delete_memory, list_canvas, delete_skill, delete_mcp_server, create_run, update_run, delete_run, delete_secret.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_memory, use_secret · Private data: delete_playbook, delete_memory, list_canvas, read_canvas, write_canvas, patch_canvas_section, get_canvas_toc, list_secrets, use_secret, store_secret, rotate_secret, delete_secret · Public sink: use_secret · Destructive: delete_playbook, delete_persona, delete_memory, list_canvas, delete_skill, delete_mcp_server, create_run, update_run, delete_run, delete_secret

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
